analysis:
This batch contains only documentation. changelog.d/cluster-auto-update.md (head 1-10) is new. It describes coordinated auto-update for two-Mac clusters. The cluster service checks the coordinator's latest release every 30 minutes at a slot derived from the cluster ID. Each Mac downloads, verifies and stages the release. The pair drains for at most 120 s. Promotion happens after 10 min healthy, and rollback/quarantine after three self-ending starts. Before restart, the new `darkbloom --version` runs once with a 30 s limit. `darkbloom update` coordinates with the partner, waiting up to 15 min. docs/architecture/inference.md head 2966-2970 adds that re-plan waits until both Macs report the same worker build (ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild).

No implementation source was supplied, so I cannot verify the following:
(1) Release download verification uses the same signed-artifact and qualification checks as the single-Mac updater (A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034, T-054).
(2) Running the new binary's --version before restart happens only after signature verification; otherwise an unverified binary would run as the owner (A-019).
(3) Rollback and quarantine authority mirrors the watchdog's, with the known limit that it is the same replaceable binary (T-043).
(4) The authenticated pair control link carries the update and drain coordination, so a partner cannot force a downgrade or an indefinite drain. Repeated drains failing at the 120 s bound could be an availability lever (A-018).
(5) Drain never cancels accepted requests, and a stale grant does not survive across the restart (T-053).

These are documentation claims about controls outside the supplied evidence, not observed regressions. Integration should examine ClusterService update/drain code if it is present in other batches. No change to prefix-cache, attestation or encryption behavior is evident in these units.
